sections.h2: What is Bryan County, Georgia like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Bryan County sits in the Savannah metropolitan area and is split in two by the Fort Stewart military installation. Pembroke, the county seat, lies in the rural north. Richmond Hill, the largest city, is a Savannah suburb in the south, and Wikipedia notes that driving between the two on public roads means leaving the county (Wikipedia). That split explains why the county runs two offices for almost every property tax service.

The county was created on December 19, 1793. Its 2020 census population was 44,738, and the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 52,062, a gain of 16.4 percent from the 2020 base. Median owner-occupied value for 2020 to 2024 is $343,200 and median household income is $103,408, both the highest among the four counties on the Census QuickFacts comparison, with 733 building permits recorded in 2025.

The Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America electric vehicle plant began production in 2024 and is the county's largest employer. Growth tied to that plant is a big reason assessments in the south end have been closely watched.

sections.h2: Where are the Bryan County property tax offices?
sections.html:
Both the assessor and the tax commissioner keep an office in Pembroke and another in Richmond Hill. The assessor values property. The commissioner bills, collects and distributes the money. The assessor's page states plainly that the office does not set the tax rate and has no part in collecting taxes.

sections.h2: When are Bryan County tax bills due and what happens if I pay late?
sections.html:
For tax year 2026, bills were mailed on October 16 and are due Tuesday, December 15, 2026. The county's property tax page says bills generally go out around September and give at least 60 days to pay, so the date can shift from year to year.

The county prints its late-payment schedule:

  • Interest of 0.875 percent for each month or part of a month starts the day after the due date.
  • A 5 percent penalty is added 120 days after the due date.
  • Another 5 percent is added after each further 120 days, capped at 20 percent in total.
  • Once a bill is 30 days delinquent, the tax commissioner, acting as ex-officio sheriff, may begin tax sale proceedings.

Georgia ties each bill to the owner of record on January 1, so a house that sold in spring still produces a bill for that year in the old owner's name unless the paperwork was sent in.

sections.h2: How does Bryan County set and appeal a home's value?
sections.html:
Fair market value is set by the assessor, and the taxable base is 40 percent of it, less any homestead exemption. The commissioner multiplies that taxable value by the millage rate, and the county posts the 2026 millage rates on its tax page.

For 2026, assessment notices were mailed on June 12 and the last day to appeal was July 27. That window has closed, and the assessor's page says late appeals are not accepted. The rules it states are worth knowing for any future year:

  • The appeal must be in writing on the county's form.
  • It must reach either the Pembroke or Richmond Hill office by 5:00 p.m. on the deadline.
  • Email and fax appeals are refused, and a postmark does not count as proof of timely filing.

The assessor's office is also photographing residential properties for record updates, and you may see a county vehicle stop briefly at your home. A new owner learns the value the year after a sale, when the first notice arrives.

sections.h2: Who pays the tax when a Bryan County house sells?
sections.html:
The commissioner's office does not prorate taxes by sale date, length of use or current ownership. That is a direct quote from its page, and it means the split between buyer and seller is handled at the closing table.

After a sale, send the tax commissioner a copy of the recorded deed and the closing documents so the next bill reaches the new owner. You can drop them at either office, mail them to P.O. Box 447, Pembroke, GA 31321, or email propertytax@bryancountyga.gov. Address changes and homestead applications go to the assessor's office rather than the commissioner.

Ask your closing attorney how the current year's bill will be divided and whether the December due date falls before or after your closing. If a bill is outstanding, request a payoff from the commissioner so it can be paid from the sale proceeds.

sections.h2: What about homestead, mobile homes and business property in Bryan County?
sections.html:
The county's own example of a homestead exemption uses a $2,000 reduction from assessed value. Applications go to the assessor, and your owner status on January 1 decides eligibility, so ask that office which exemptions fit your age, income or veteran status.

Mobile homes follow separate billing rules. A non-homestead mobile home is billed in January and due April 1. A mobile home with a homestead exemption is taxed together with its land, and that bill is due around November 15. Before a mobile home is moved, even out of the county, all taxes must be paid and you need a paid receipt.

Business owners file a personal property return with the assessor by April 1 every year they operate. If no return is filed, state-established values are used. Timber sales must be reported on Department of Revenue form PT-283T, and heavy-duty equipment bought from a dealer is taxed in the year of purchase.

faqs.q: When are 2026 property taxes due in Bryan County?
faqs.a: The 2026 bills are due Tuesday, December 15, 2026. They were mailed on October 16. After the due date, interest of 0.875 percent per month applies.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal my 2026 Bryan County assessment?
faqs.a: No. The 2026 deadline was 5:00 p.m. on July 27, and the assessor's office says late appeals are not accepted. Watch for the next notice and file in writing within 45 days of its date.

faqs.q: Does Bryan County prorate property tax when a house sells?
faqs.a: No. The tax commissioner's office states that it does not prorate by sale date. The buyer and seller divide the bill at closing, so ask your closing attorney to handle it.

faqs.q: Where do I send my deed after selling a Bryan County property?
faqs.a: Send the recorded deed and closing documents to the Bryan County Tax Commissioner, P.O. Box 447, Pembroke, GA 31321, or to propertytax@bryancountyga.gov. You can also drop them at the Pembroke or Richmond Hill office.

faqs.q: What happens if I do not pay Bryan County property tax?
faqs.a: Interest and penalties build, with penalties capped at 20 percent. After 30 days of delinquency the tax commissioner may begin tax sale proceedings, so contact the office early if you cannot pay in full.
